scenes.heading: Writing a listing that actually attracts buyers

sents.d: Writing a listing that actually attracts buyers
Specific, honest details usually outperform generic superlatives.

Generic listing language ('must see,' 'won't last') is largely ignored by buyers who see it in every listing — specific, concrete details (actual square footage, specific recent updates, genuine standout features) are far more persuasive.
Professional photography is one of the highest-leverage investments in a listing, since most buyers form their first impression from photos online long before ever seeing a property in person.

Being honest about a property's real limitations in showings and conversations, rather than only in the fine print, tends to build more trust with buyers and reduces the likelihood of a deal falling apart over a late 'surprise.'

take: Write specific listings, use great photos and be upfront.
